page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, delivering four vCPUs derived from two dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside support for AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance is allocated 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM general-purpose ratio.

Hardware integration excludes bundled local storage and graphics acceleration, meaning external block storage volumes must be attached for operational persistence. Network capabilities are defined by a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth rating, with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. Memory subsystem benchmarks show uncached read speeds of 21.08 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 18.75 GB/sec.

Performance across synthetic and application benchmarks consistently places the instance in the lower tier relative to modern cloud hardware. Geekbench multi-core registers at 2175.0, while stress-ng multi-core yields 2936.9. Core system operations, such as single-threaded gzip compression at 19.17 GB/sec and static web serving throughput of 3.36 GB/sec, align with legacy Skylake-generation execution profiles.

From an infrastructure and cost efficiency perspective, ecs.g5.xlarge offers dedicated execution cores without burst credits, preventing compute throttling during continuous execution. However, the throughput-per-core tradeoffs reflect older generation hardware. The instance is suited for lightweight enterprise middleware, non-critical web serving, staging environments, and balanced standard background tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration supplies 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 16.0 GB of memory, and AVX-512 instruction support, maintaining a balanced 1:4 compute-to-RAM ratio. No local storage or discrete GPUs are integrated into the profile, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Across benchmark evaluations, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and memory throughput tests, the system demonstrates lower-tier compute and memory performance consistent with older generation platforms. Given its dedicated resource allocation and balanced hardware profile, the instance suits lightweight web applications, development environments, and moderate microservice deployments that do not require high single-thread speeds.
